headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell execution create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; AutoGen’s configurable isolation is not enabled by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write working directories and xonsh can read/write the filesystem, so a shared workspace can carry attacker-controlled instructions from agent_a into agent_b. No MCP or clipboard bridge is shown, so this is not high, but the interaction exists in default-style shared-file workflows.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b are configured to share the same working directory, prompt injection via files is possible.
IF agent_b parses file contents as commands or instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer execution.
mitigations: Use separate working directories for each agent.
Disable automatic execution of file contents in agent_b.
Add a manual review step before agent_b consumes agent_a outputs.
Prefix agent_a outputs with a non-executable delimiter format.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch filesystem contents and both have broad network egress, so sensitive application data passed to agent_a can be exposed through shared files or outbound requests from either side. AutoGen’s isolation is configurable rather than default-enforced, while xonsh also reads environment and notebook content, increasing leakage surface.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same workspace, file-based leakage is possible.
IF agent_a or agent_b sends workspace contents to configured model providers or APIs, sensitive data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.
Restrict outbound network access for one agent during shared tasks.
Redact secrets before passing files between agents.
Review environment variables before launching xonsh.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and shell execution, so concurrent edits to the same directory can overwrite each other or corrupt state. AutoGen supports multiple instances and developer-defined shared state, while xonsh does not support multiple instances, making coordination weaker and conflict risk high.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF both agents modify the same scripts or notebooks without locking, race conditions can corrupt work products.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Have only one agent perform edits at a time.
Use git patches instead of direct writes where possible.
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestrator that can emit tool-driven outputs, and xonsh can execute shell commands and Python expressions. If agent_b treats agent_a’s output as authoritative, a mistaken plan or malformed command can cascade into real actions or destructive shell execution.
conditions: IF agent_b executes commands derived from agent_a output without verification, errors can cascade into system changes.
IF agent_a produces incorrect file paths or commands, agent_b may act on them directly.
mitigations: Require human review before execution.
Validate commands against an allowlist.
Have agent_b summarize and restate agent_a output before acting.
Run a dry-run mode first.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent messages.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles show broad filesystem and network access, but only agent_a explicitly lists model-provider API keys and configurable isolation; agent_b is unverified and its compliance posture is undocumented. The main issue is a likely retention/residency mismatch for application data, but the evidence is indirect rather than direct.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, retention and residency obligations may be violated.
IF agent_b forwards notebook or filesystem contents to external services, compliance controls may be bypassed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Confirm retention settings for both agents.
Disable external API calls for regulated tasks.
Document data flow ownership before use.
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance review.
